Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Reno NV
136 AM PST Mon Nov 23 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

* Cold temperatures and areas of freezing fog this morning,
  followed by mostly dry weather today through Tuesday afternoon.

* A weak storm brings increased winds and light Sierra snow 
  Tuesday night into Wednesday morning. 

* Dry and mild weather is favored for Thanksgiving Day, with
  additional storms possible late next weekend and beyond. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...

Clearing skies and light showers from Sunday evening will support
pockets of freezing fog across NE California and E Sierra valleys
this morning -- including along I-80 near Truckee. Be prepared 
for reduced visibilities and slick roads during this morning's 
commute in these areas before fog mixes out around 9-10 AM PST. 
Today through much of Tuesday will offer dry weather and cool 
temperatures beneath transient high pressure. This will be the 
most ideal window for trans-Sierra travel before light snow 
returns Tuesday night...

A quick upper trough passage will increase shower chances along 
the Sierra from Lassen County to the Tahoe Basin Tuesday evening 
through Wednesday morning. This storm will be a rather weak one, 
providing up to 1" of snow along the Sierra crest and at pass 
level. Even the "snowier" scenarios (10% chance) only show 2-4" 
along highest peaks and along Donner Pass by midday Wednesday. 
Truckee and Lake Tahoe communities may see, at most, a trace of 
snow on grassy and elevated surfaces early Wednesday (10% odds). 
While major travel impacts are not anticipated, those traveling 
through the Sierra should be prepared for slick roads near 
summits. Dry conditions are favored for Mono County and W Nevada 
communities where showers are shadowed out. 

Winds begin to increase on Tuesday as the trough approaches, 
yielding SW gusts of 25-35 mph near the Oregon border and 20-30 mph 
gusts across E Sierra valleys Tuesday afternoon. Ridgetop winds may 
gust up to 80 mph at times. Expect wind impacts to backcountry and 
lake recreation, with turbulent flights into and out of regional 
airports Tuesday into Wednesday morning. 

Aside from a low 10-20% chance of rain near the Oregon border, 
Thanksgiving Day is shaping up to be dry and mild as high pressure 
overspreads the region. Daytime highs are slated to be in the upper 
40s and 50s, followed by chilly nighttime lows in the 20s and 30s 
early Friday morning. Dry weather prevails Friday and much of 
Saturday before the potential for another storm increases Sunday 
into Monday, posing impacts to post-holiday travel plans. This 
storm has a warmer look with higher snow levels keeping snow in 
the mountains and rain in the valleys. Ensembles suggest that 
we'll remain in a stormy pattern next week, but hard to have much 
confidence at this extended range. 

-Salas

&&

.AVIATION...

KRNO Forecast: VFR conditions and light breezes prevail today into 
Tuesday. Mid to high level clouds begin to increase this afternoon 
ahead of an approaching weak storm. 

Regional Outlook: FZFG will lead to periods of LIFR conditions at 
KTRK through 16-17Z this morning. Otherwise, VFR conditions and 
light breezes prevail through Tuesday morning.   

24-72 Hour Outlook: A weak Pacific storm will increase winds and 
bring light snow showers to Tahoe terminals Tuesday night and 
Wednesday morning. A 20-40% chance of -SN at KTRK-KTVL may reduce 
CIGS/VIS to MVFR conditions Tuesday night into Wednesday morning. SW 
FL100 flow increases to around 35 kts Tuesday afternoon from Tahoe 
northward, posing LLWS and mountain wave turbulence impacts at KTRK-
KTVL and KRNO-KCXP-KMEV into Tuesday night. 

-Salas
